question: In Brazil, coffee plantations are known as:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Fazenda**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In Brazil, coffee plantations are known as **Fazenda**.
 
• A **Fazenda** is a large plantation or estate found throughout Brazil, typically one that grows coffee, sugarcane, or other crops.
 
• The term **Fazenda** is derived from the Portuguese word for "farm" or "estate".
 
• Brazil is one of the largest producers of coffee in the world, and its **Fazendas** play a crucial role in this industry.
 
• These plantations often span large areas and incorporate both traditional and modern farming techniques.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Coffee cultivation** in Brazil began in the 18th century and has since grown to become a significant part of the country's economy.
 
• The regions of **Minas Gerais, São Paulo, and Espírito Santo** are known for their extensive coffee plantations.
 
• Brazilian coffee is renowned for its high quality, and the country exports a substantial portion of its production to various parts of the world.
 
• The coffee industry in Brazil provides employment to millions of people and contributes significantly to rural development.
 
• Efforts are being made to promote sustainable farming practices on **Fazendas** to ensure the long-term viability of coffee production in Brazil.
